question: Which drive models account for most of the change in the Backblaze fleet's annualized failure rate from Q1 2026 to Q2 2026?
truth_sql: WITH w AS (SELECT model, CASE WHEN day <= DATE '2026-03-31' THEN 'a' ELSE 'b' END AS p, failure FROM drive_day WHERE source = 'backblaze' AND (day BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-03-31' OR day BETWEEN DATE '2026-04-01' AND DATE '2026-06-30')), m AS (SELECT model, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p = 'a') AS dd_a, COALESCE(SUM(failure) FILTER (WHERE p = 'a'), 0) AS f_a, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p = 'b') AS dd_b, COALESCE(SUM(failure) FILTER (WHERE p = 'b'), 0) AS f_b FROM w GROUP BY model), fleet AS (SELECT SUM(dd_a) AS dd_a, SUM(f_a) AS f_a, SUM(dd_b) AS dd_b, SUM(f_b) AS f_b FROM m), c AS (SELECT m.model, m.f_b - m.dd_b * CASE WHEN m.dd_a > 0 THEN CAST(m.f_a AS DOUBLE) / m.dd_a ELSE CAST(fleet.f_a AS DOUBLE) / fleet.dd_a END AS excess, fleet.f_b - fleet.dd_b * CAST(fleet.f_a AS DOUBLE) / fleet.dd_a AS fleet_excess FROM m, fleet), r AS (SELECT model, fleet_excess, SIGN(fleet_excess) * excess AS contrib, COALESCE(SUM(SIGN(fleet_excess) * excess) OVER ( ORDER BY SIGN(fleet_excess) * excess DESC, model ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), 0) AS cum_before FROM c) SELECT COALESCE(list(r.model ORDER BY r.contrib DESC, r.model) FILTER (WHERE r.contrib > 0 AND r.cum_before < 0.5 * ABS(r.fleet_excess)), CAST([] AS VARCHAR[])) AS truth_set, list(r.model ORDER BY r.model) AS candidates, ANY_VALUE(r.fleet_excess) AS fleet_excess_failures, ANY_VALUE(CAST(fleet.f_a AS DOUBLE) * 365 * 100 / fleet.dd_a) AS fleet_afr_pct_earlier, ANY_VALUE(CAST(fleet.f_b AS DOUBLE) * 365 * 100 / fleet.dd_b) AS fleet_afr_pct_later FROM r, fleet
notes: Truth set: models sorted by excess failures (later-period failures minus later drive days times the model's earlier rate, fleet rate if new), smallest prefix whose sum reaches 50% of the fleet's excess; signs flip when the fleet AFR fell. Check: the direction of the fleet change, and that no model with a tiny earlier cohort dominates because of an unstable earlier rate.
